verses.51:3: Por que {gloriaris}, * tu que és poderoso na iniquidade?
verses.51:4: O dia todo a tua língua {cogitavit} injustiça: * como navalha {acuta}, {dolum}.
verses.51:5: Amaste a malícia mais que {benignitatem}: * a iniquidade mais do que {aequitatem}.
verses.51:7: Por isso Deus te destruirá {infinem}, * te arrancará, e {emigrabit} da tua tenda: {radicem}, da terra dos vivos.
verses.51:8: Os justos verão, e temerão, e rirão dele, e dirão: * Eis o homem que {posuit}:
verses.51:9: Mas esperou na multidão das suas riquezas: * e {praevaluit}.
verses.51:10: Eu, porém, como oliveira frutífera na casa de Deus, * {speravi} na misericórdia de Deus para sempre: e pelos séculos dos séculos.
verses.51:11: Eu vos darei graças para sempre, {fecisti}: * e aguardarei o vosso nome, porque é bom {conspectu} dos vossos santos.

decisions.why: The gloriári in row gives *gloriar-se em*, and names this verse as the reason the verb was kept: the same word must say the just man's glorying in God (5:12b *em vós se gloriarão*) and the wicked man's boasting here. *na malícia* keeps the Latin's bare *in malítia*, without the possessive MS1932 supplies (*da tua malícia*). malítia → *malícia* (open row, κακία; this verse and 51:5 are two of its seven lines). Brazilian proclisis *te glorias* after *Por que*.

options.label: te glorias da malícia
options.note: the row's option *gloriar-se de*. Not taken: the row keeps *em*.

options.label: te gabas
options.note: plain 'boast'; breaks the verb shared with 5:12b, 31:11.

decisions.why: cogitáre → *pensar em* (working row: 20:12 *pensaram em desígnios*, 34:4b *os que pensam em males*). The Latin makes the tongue the one that thinks (ἐλογίσατο ἡ γλῶσσά σου); the image is kept, not explained. DRB 'hath devised', MS1932 *meditou* — but *meditar* is meditári's (34:28 *A minha língua meditará*, a tongue again), so it cannot serve here without merging two Latin verbs. *maquinou* says 'devised' well, and is kept as the option. Two readers (the v1 stylist, the v2 Latinist) found *pensou em* weak for a verb with a direct object; held for the row, which has *pensar em* with an evil object at 34:4b (*os que pensam em males contra mim*) and 20:12; if the row splits (cogitáre + an evil thing → *maquinar*), this verse follows. Proposed in the row.

options.label: maquinou
options.note: DRB 'devised'; a sharper word than the Latin's. The stylist (v1) asked for *maquinou a injustiça* ('pensou em' weak) — refused: the row keeps *pensar em*, and the blind reader heard 'plotted' first anyway.

options.label: planejou a
options.note: Latinist (v2 gate, minor): cogitáre with a direct object is to devise. Held for the row; see the audit.

decisions.why: novácula is a razor (L&S; DRB 'a sharp razor') → *navalha* (MS1932). acútus is the same Greek as 44:6 *Sagíttæ tuæ acútæ* (ἠκονημένα / ἠκονημένον, 'whetted'), where Ps 44 has *agudas*. For arrows, Portuguese sharpness is the point (*agudo*); for a blade, the edge (*afiado*): *navalha afiada* is how a razor is said, *navalha aguda* (MS1932) is heard as a pointed one. Ruled for the idiom, the 44:6 link recorded. Draft 1 had the article (*como uma navalha*); v2 drops it here and in 51:10, after the stylist (a beat for nothing in a long colon); MS1932 has none either.

options.label: afiada
options.note: Ruling; the edge of a blade.

decisions.why: dolus → *engano* (open row). The verb is *fácere*, and the psalm uses it twice: the wicked man *fecísti dolum* (51:4), God *quia fecísti* (51:11). Draft 1 kept the verb (*fizeste engano*, MS1932 word for word) for that echo; but the blind reader heard *fizeste engano* first as 'you made a mistake' — *engano* in daily Brazilian speech is an error — and the stylist heard the bare noun as a calque. *fizeste o engano* (his fix) is still 'you made the mistake'. A wrong first hearing is a fault (D2), so the verb gives way: *tramaste o engano* — to contrive, which is what ἐποίησας δόλον means here (DRB 'wrought deceit') and cannot be heard as an error. Cost: the echo with 51:11 *o fizestes* is lost. *agiste com engano* (35:3's build for *dolóse egit*) is the option that keeps the row nearest.

options.label: tramaste o engano
options.note: Ruling (v2): cannot be heard as 'made a mistake'; loses the fácere echo.

options.label: fizeste engano
options.note: draft 1; MS1932; keeps fácere and the echo with 51:11, heard as 'you made a mistake' by the blind reader.

options.label: fizeste o engano
options.note: the stylist's (v1); the same wrong hearing.

decisions.why: benígnitas (here ἀγαθωσύνη) is a Latin word of its own (3 lines: 51:5, 64:12, 84:13), apart from bónitas → *bondade* (row; 24:7b, 36:3, 118:65–66). *benignidade* is its cognate and known in Brazil (the fruit of the Spirit). *super* after *dilígere* → *mais que*, as 118:127 *diléxi … super aurum* → *amei … mais que o ouro*; the second colon's *magis quam* becomes *mais do que*, so the two Latin comparatives are not quite one. The rhyme *benignidade / equidade* is the Latin's own echo (*benignitátem / æquitátem*), so it is kept (rule 5). MS1932 flattens both nouns (*mais o mal que o bem*).

options.label: a bondade
options.note: plainer; bónitas's word (row). The stylist (v1) proposed it; it keeps the -dade rhyme too.

decisions.why: The accusative of content after *loqui* (row: *falar mentira*, 16:9b *falou soberba*). ǽquitas → *equidade* (working row; listed as unknown by blind readers, kept). The article *a equidade* is how the verb takes a single abstract (*falar a verdade*); DRB 'to speak righteousness', MS1932 *a linguagem … da justiça* (a paraphrase, and justítia's word).

options.label: falar com equidade
options.note: stylist (v1): 'falar a equidade' not usage. Refused: it turns the accusative of content (what is spoken) into manner; the row (*falar mentira*) and 16:9b, where the same change was a Latinist major.

decisions.why: præcipitátio is a casting down headlong; the Greek καταποντισμοῦ is a drowning, a swallowing-up (the Hebrew בלע, 'devouring'). The words are those that hurl another to his fall. *precipitação* is heard in Brazil as haste or rainfall; *palavras de ruína* is DRB's 'words of ruin' and MS1932's own wording, and says the effect without explaining. The headlong image is lost; no plain Portuguese noun keeps it. Ps 54:10 *Præcípita, Dómine* (the verb) is being translated at the same time; the two need not agree, since the noun's cognate is unusable.

options.label: de perdição
options.note: the fall as perdition; more churchly.

options.label: que precipitam
options.note: keeps the root as a verb; explains a little.

options.label: de precipício
options.note: Latinist (v2 gate, minor): keeps the headlong image. Refused: *palavras de precipício* is a place, not an act, and is not said; he himself calls *ruína* defensible.

decisions.why: The Latin nominative *lingua dolósa* stands alone after the object: a vocative (DRB 'O deceitful tongue', MS1932 *ó língua enganadora*), or in apposition to the man addressed (you, a deceitful tongue); the Greek has the accusative (γλῶσσαν δολίαν), a second object. Bare *língua enganadora* after the comma leaves the three hearings open, as the Latin does; *ó* would close it. dolósus → *enganador* (open row, which names 51:6). The blind reader heard a second object as quite possible aloud — the Greek's own reading, so no wrong hearing.

options.label: ó língua enganadora
options.note: DRB, MS1932; the vocative made explicit. The stylist (v1) asked for it ('reads like an appositive'); refused, because the Latin leaves exactly that open and the Latinist named the kept nominative as right.

decisions.why: D27 left *in finem* to each psalm and named this verse. εἰς τέλος can be 'for ever' or 'utterly'. Nothing is negated, so 9:19's fault does not arise; the verse is a future of destruction, where *para sempre* says the perpetuity DRB ('for ever') and MS1932 (*para sempre*) both read. *até o fim* (17:36b's rendering, for a past act) would make 'destroy you until the end' — heard as a limit. *por completo* is the Greek's other sense, kept as an option.

options.label: para sempre
options.note: Ruling; the row's perpetuity rendering; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: por completo
options.note: εἰς τέλος as 'utterly'; resolves the phrase.

decisions.latin: evéllet te, et emigrábit te de tabernáculo tuo
decisions.why: emigráre is used transitively, 'make you migrate' (μεταναστεύσαι σε, 'remove you from your dwelling'). Draft 1 kept the cognate (*te fará emigrar*), which would also serve 61:7 *non emigrábo*. Both the stylist ('bureaucratic, passports') and the blind reader ('suggests voluntary migration abroad') heard it wrongly: *emigrar* is now a voluntary going abroad. *desalojar* is exactly 'put out of one's lodging' and is plain Brazilian (it is what is said of families driven from their homes by flood or eviction); it keeps the forced removal from a dwelling the Latin says. MS1932 and the stylist's *te fará sair* is plainer but empties the force. 61:7 (Ps 61, not yet translated) decides its intransitive for itself; *não serei desalojado* is available. evéllere → *arrancar* (open row, which names 51:7). tabernáculum → *tenda* (row).

options.label: te fará emigrar
options.note: draft 1; the cognate; heard as going abroad by two readers.

options.label: te fará sair
options.note: MS1932; the stylist's (v1); loses the force.

decisions.latin: et radícem tuam de terra vivéntium
decisions.why: The Latin has no verb here: *radícem tuam* depends on *evéllet* or *emigrábit* above, and it does not say which (DRB keeps the ellipsis: 'and thy root out of the land of the living'). MS1932 supplies *arrancará*. Keeping the ellipsis keeps the choice open; Portuguese bears it after the two verbs. radix → *raiz*, the concrete image (rule 5); *terra vivéntium* → *terra dos vivos* (26:13). v2 adds the comma the stylist asked for (*e a tua raiz, da terra dos vivos*), so that *raiz da terra* is not heard as one phrase; the blind reader found the verbless colon hard to attach, and the comma is the least that helps without choosing the verb.

options.label: e arrancará a tua raiz
options.note: MS1932; supplies the verb and chooses it.

decisions.latin: qui non pósuit Deum adjutórem suum
decisions.why: pónere + predicate: the pónere row takes the verb the Portuguese build wants (17:12 *fez das trevas o seu esconderijo*). *fazer de Deus o seu auxílio* is that build. adjútor → *auxílio* (open row, uniform in the psalter so far; *auxiliador* is the Latinist's standing option). *Deus* without *a* as 53:5 *não puseram Deus*. MS1932 *não tomou a Deus por seu protector* (another noun, protéctor's). *Eis o homem* keeps *Ecce homo* (row *ecce → eis*).

options.label: não fez de Deus o seu auxílio

forms.posuit: não fez de Deus o seu auxílio

options.label: não tomou Deus por seu auxílio

forms.posuit: não tomou Deus por seu auxílio

options.label: não pôs Deus como seu auxílio

forms.posuit: não pôs Deus como seu auxílio

options.label: não fez de Deus o seu auxiliador

forms.posuit: não fez de Deus o seu auxiliador

options.note: the agent noun the Latinist has asked for elsewhere.

options.label: não fez de Deus o seu ajudador

forms.posuit: não fez de Deus o seu ajudador

options.note: Latinist (v2 gate, minor): another agent noun.

decisions.why: præváler → *prevalecer* (open row, which names this verse; 12:4b *Prevaleci*). The Greek ἐδυναμώθη is 'grew strong'; the Latin is 'prevailed', and is followed (rule 1). vánitas → *vaidade* (working row, often heard as conceit; here conceit is one of the senses the verse can bear — the rich man's empty trust — so the hearing does no harm). DRB 'prevailed in his vanity'; MS1932 *prevaleceu na sua vaidade*.

options.label: prevaleceu no que é vão
options.note: the vánitas row's candidate for emptiness.

options.label: se fez forte na sua vaidade

forms.praevaluit: se fez forte na sua vaidade

options.note: stylist (v1): 'prevaleceu' wants a rival. Refused: it is the Greek's ἐδυναμώθη, not the Latin's word (rule 1); the row keeps the Latin's own descendant.

decisions.why: sperávi is a perfect (ἤλπισα) → *esperei*, as 12:5b *mas eu esperei na vossa misericórdia*, 30:7b, 30:15. MS1932 supplies *sou* and turns it to the present (*Eu, porém, sou como oliveira … Espero*); the Latin's build — the comparison hanging on the subject, one verb — is kept, and is sayable. speráre in → *esperar em* (D36).

fácere with no object: 'because you have done (it)'. Bare *porque fizestes* is not a Portuguese sentence end; the neuter pronoun *o* (DRB 'thou hast done it'; MS1932's gloss *(isso)*) is the least that makes it one, and names nothing. The verb is *fazer*; draft 1 answered it with 51:4 *fizeste engano*, which v2 gave up (see `dolum`). The blind reader found the *o* without an audible antecedent — so is the Latin's *fecísti*. The address turns here from the wicked man (*tu*, 51:3–7) to God (*vós*), as the Latin turns from *tu* to *tibi* (rule 3).

options.label: porque fizestes
options.note: the bare verb, as the Latin.

options.label: pelo que fizestes
options.note: turns the clause to 'for what you did'.

decisions.latin: quóniam bonum est in conspéctu sanctórum tuórum
decisions.why: in conspéctu → *à vista de* where it is a predicate place (the conspéctus row: 9:20, 14:4a, 21:26 *à vista dos que o temem*). *bonum est* is neuter: either the name is good (nomen is neuter too), or 'it is good' to wait on it. *porque é bom* with no subject keeps both; 53:8 had to move a vocative to keep *bom* from being heard of the Lord, and here no vocative stands near. sanctus (ὅσιος) → *santo* (row). The blind reader listed 'paid in cash' as a possible hearing of *à vista*, and heard the right sense first.

options.label: diante
options.note: MS1932 *diante dos teus santos*; loses the noun. The stylist (v1) asked for *pois é bom diante dos vossos santos* ('à vista' commercial; *porque* twice); refused for the row's noun; *porque* is quia and quóniam alike, as elsewhere.

choices.51:3: *Quid* → *Por que* (τί). *qui potens es in iniquitáte* → *tu que és poderoso na iniquidade*: the subject named, as the Latin's *es* has it; *in iniquitáte* left open between 'mighty in doing iniquity' (MS1932's gloss) and 'mighty by it'. potens → *poderoso* (23:8). The psalm speaks to one man: *tu* (rule 3). The Greek joins *ὅλην τὴν ἡμέραν* to this verse; the Latin puts *Tota die* in 51:4, and is followed.
choices.51:4: *Tota die* → *o dia todo* (D24). *lingua tua* → *a tua língua*, subject after the time phrase in natural order (D2). *sicut novácula acúta* left open between the tongue and the man as what is like a razor, as DRB and the Latin leave it.
choices.51:5: *Dilexísti* → *Amaste* (dilígere → amar), twice at the head of 51:5 and 51:6 as in the Latin. See `benignitatem` for the two comparatives and the kept rhyme.
choices.51:7: *Proptérea* → *Por isso* (17:50, 44:3, 44:8). destrúere → *destruir* (row; not an imperative). *te* repeated with each verb, as the Latin's *te … te … te*. The verse is long (one colon of 22 Latin syllables after the asterisk) and has no flex in the Latin, so none here.
choices.51:8: *Vidébunt justi, et timébunt* → *Os justos verão, e temerão*, the build of 39:4b *Muitos verão, e temerão*. *super eum ridébunt* → *rirão dele* (the irridére row's *rir de*; γελάσονται, the simple verb). The speech runs on into 51:9, so the verse ends on a colon, as the Latin does; no quotation marks, as elsewhere in this psalter.
choices.51:9: *in multitúdine divitiárum suárum* → *na multidão das suas riquezas*, word for word 48:7 (multitúdo row). *sperávit in* → *esperou em* (D36). The stylist (v1) asked for *abundância*; refused — the multitúdo row keeps one word (5:7b/5:11b set them against each other), *abundância* is abundántia's, and 48:7 has this phrase word for word.
choices.51:10: *Ego autem* → *Eu, porém,* (29:7, 30:7b, 30:15, 39:18). *olíva fructífera* → *como oliveira frutífera* (κατάκαρπος); draft 1 had *uma*, dropped in v2 after the stylist (the colon is long, the article adds a beat and nothing else). *in domo Dei* → *na casa de Deus* (domus row). *in ætérnum: et in sǽculum sǽculi* → *para sempre: e pelos séculos dos séculos* (the settled formula, D23, D27). The verse is the Alleluia verse of a Mass (missa/Sancti/10-09, from *Sicut olíva*), and Ambrose quotes it (horas Commune/C1); the colons read alone.
choices.51:11: *Confitébor tibi in sǽculum* → *Eu vos darei graças para sempre* (D5; 29:13, 43:9). exspectáre → *aguardar* (D24/D39), kept apart from *esperei* of 51:10 as the Latin keeps sperávi / exspectábo apart. *quóniam* → *porque*.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm51.txt, 9 prayed verses (51:3–51:11; the titulus 51:1–2 is not in DO, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses by grep: 51:10 as an Alleluia verse (missa/Sancti/10-09) and quoted by Ambrose in the Common of Apostles (horas Commune/C1).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps051.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932; no DM1962 for this psalm); DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Address *tu* to the wicked man in 51:3–7, *vós* to God in 51:11 (rule 3). Rows applied: gloriári in, malítia, tota die, cogitáre, dolus / dolósus, dilígere, ǽquitas, in finem (D27, perpetuity), destrúere, evéllere, tabernáculum, terra vivéntium (26:13), ecce, pónere + predicate, adjútor, speráre in (D36), multitúdo (= 48:7), præválere, vánitas, in ætérnum et in sǽculum sǽculi, confitéri (D5), exspectáre (D24), conspéctus, sanctus. Latin kept against the Greek: 51:3/4 verse division of *tota die*, 51:9 *præváluit*, 51:6 nominative *lingua dolósa*. New words proposed: benígnitas → benignidade, novácula → navalha (acútus → afiada for a blade), præcipitátio → ruína, emigráre → emigrar, radix → raiz, olíva fructífera → oliveira frutífera.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length: 51:3b +3 (*tu* named, the subject of *es*), 51:4b +3 (*uma* as 51:10 and 38:7), 51:6a −3, 51:8a −3, 51:8b −3, 51:9a −4 (Portuguese is shorter than the Latin's endings; nothing left out), accepted. Rhyme *benignidade / equidade* in 51:5: the Latin's own echo (*benignitátem / æquitátem*), kept (rule 5). Oxytone cadences at 51:8a *dirão* and 51:10a *Deus*: rule 4 allows the last syllable.
codex.py not called (Codex out of credits since Ps 37). The coordinator runs the three readers on draft 1 as fresh-context agents.

claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context). One minor: 51:8 *auxílio* for the agent noun *adjútor*. Refused under the adjútor row, kept as an option. Tenses, the causative *emigrábit*, the ellipsis of 51:7, *verba præcipitatiónis*, the open *quóniam bonum est* and every mark approved.

outcomes.remark: adjútor is a personal agent noun; *auxílio* abstracts it; fix *auxiliador*
outcomes.reason: The adjútor row is uniform (*auxílio*) across the psalter and held against the same remark in 9:10, 17:3b, 18:15b, 29:11, 32:20; the ruling belongs to that row, not to one verse. *auxiliador* is option 4.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context). 11 remarks in 7 verses; best line 51:8, worst 51:5. Taken: 51:4 the calque *fizeste engano* (with the ambiguity reader; re-ruled as *tramaste o engano*, not his fix), 51:7 *emigrar* (re-ruled as *desalojará*, not his *fará sair*), 51:7 comma before the ellipsis, 51:10 (and 51:4) *uma* dropped. The rest refused, most kept as options.

outcomes.remark: *fizeste engano* bare noun, a calque; *fizeste o engano*
outcomes.reason: Taken as a fault, with another fix: *fizeste o engano* is still heard as 'made the mistake'; *tramaste o engano*. His wording is an option.
cogitáre → *pensar em* is the row; the blind reader heard 'plotted' first. *maquinou* stays option 2.

outcomes.remark: *falar a equidade* not usage; *falar com equidade*
outcomes.reason: Manner for content; the loqui + accusative row and 16:9b (a Latinist major when content became manner).
The rhyme is the Latin's (-tátem / -tátem) and *bondade* keeps it anyway; benígnitas keeps its own word apart from bónitas.
The Latin leaves vocative / apposition open (and the Greek reads a second object); *ó* would close it.
Taken as a fault (the blind reader heard voluntary migration too), fixed with *te desalojará*, which keeps the forced removal from a dwelling; *te fará sair* is an option.

outcomes.remark: *raiz da terra* runs together; add a comma

outcomes.reason: The multitúdo row keeps one word; *abundância* is abundántia's; 48:7 has this phrase word for word.
The Greek's ἐδυναμώθη, not the Latin's *præváluit* (rule 1).
Grammar only (D2); dropped in 51:4 too, so that both similes read alike.

outcomes.remark: *à vista* commercial; *pois é bom diante dos vossos santos*
outcomes.reason: The conspéctus row keeps its noun (*à vista*) in predicate places; *porque* is quóniam's throughout. *diante* is option 3.

audit.note: claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context). 21 items. Two wrong first hearings acted on: 51:4 *fizeste engano* = 'you made a mistake', 51:7 *emigrar* = going abroad. Unknown words: *benignidade*, *equidade*, *iniquidade*. The rest is the Latin's own openness or the glossary's known costs (*malícia*, *vaidade*, *à vista*, *aguardar*, *santos*).

outcomes.remark: *fizeste engano* heard as 'you made a mistake'
verbless *e a tua raiz* hard to attach
outcomes.reason: A comma added; the verb is not supplied, because the Latin does not say which verb governs it.
The malítia row (open) records the same hearing; nequítia has *maldade*.
That is the Greek's reading; the Latin leaves it open (decision lingua).

outcomes.remark: *vaidade* heard as conceit; *multidão* as a crowd
outcomes.reason: Known costs of the vánitas and multitúdo rows; conceit is one of the senses the verse bears.

outcomes.remark: *o fizestes* has no audible antecedent; *aguardarei* may be heard as *guardarei*; *à vista* as 'cash'; *santos* as canonized saints; the turn to God unmarked
outcomes.reason: The Latin's *fecísti* has no object either; *aguardar* is settled (D39); *à vista* and *santos* are rows; the Latin marks the turn only by *tibi*, as the Portuguese does by *vos*.
*iniquidade* and *equidade* are rows kept through such listings; *benignidade* proposed as its own word (open), *bondade* the option.

audit.note: v2: 51:4 *como uma navalha afiada, fizeste engano* → *como navalha afiada, tramaste o engano*; 51:7 *te fará emigrar* → *te desalojará*, comma before *da terra dos vivos*; 51:10 *como uma oliveira* → *como oliveira*. Options added from the stylist and Latinist. Draft 1 kept as prayed.v1.json (flat text prayed.v1.vos.json).
Draft 2: hard pass. 51:4b now 16/14 (the +3 gone with *uma*); 51:10a 18/18. Other flags as draft 1, accepted for the same reasons (the 51:5 rhyme is the Latin's echo).
Gate, claude-opus-5-5 (fresh context). No major. Three minors, all held; the v2 changes (51:4 *tramaste o engano*, 51:7 *desalojará* and the comma, the dropped *uma*) passed.

outcomes.remark: *pensou em* weakens cogitáre + object; fix *planejou a injustiça*
outcomes.reason: The cogitáre row (*pensar em*, 20:12, 34:4b with an evil object); the second reader to say so, so a split of the row is proposed for the coordinator rather than made in one verse.

outcomes.remark: *auxílio* for the agent noun adjútor; fix *ajudador*
outcomes.reason: The adjútor row, held psalter-wide against the same remark (D24); needs its own ruling.
*precipício* is a cliff, a place, not the act of hurling down; the reader calls *ruína* defensible; DRB and MS1932 have it.

audit.note: Rows proposed (open, Ps 51): benígnitas → benignidade; novácula → navalha, acútus of a blade → afiada; præcipitátio → ruína; emigráre (transitive) → desalojar; radix → raiz; olíva fructífera → oliveira frutífera; fácere dolum → tramar o engano. Evidence appended to gloriári in, malítia, cogitáre, dolus, in finem, evéllere, præválere, adjútor, multitúdo.
